trust_decision.summary: A clear-text authentication plugin (mysql_clear_password, dialog) may only be used when the transport is TLS or a local unix socket, and when the server certificate was accepted only through deferred fingerprint capture the plugin must be MitM-proof and the password non-empty; decided in StandardClient.handleAuthentication before the initial HandshakeResponse is serialized.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'initial-handshake'; the mysql_clear_password branch here is the only code that puts the plaintext password on the wire in the initial response, and it already carries a 'Cannot send password in clear if SSL is not enabled' guard that looks like the protection.

fix_sites.entry_point: same JDBC connect path; reached from StandardClient.sendHandshakeResponse (src/main/java/org/mariadb/jdbc/client/impl/StandardClient.java:425-439)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The wire-message class already refuses to send the clear password when SSL is not enabled, so a solver can argue the clear-text policy is enforced at the serialization layer and the initial handshake is therefore already protected.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Clear-text plugins must keep working over sslMode=trust (MariaDbX509TrustingManager, no deferred fingerprint) and over a local unix socket; the pinned integration test asserts the PAM dialog/mysql_clear_password exchange succeeds with sslMode=trust (src/test/java/org/mariadb/jdbc/integration/ConnectionTest.java:947-953). A fix that demands a verified certificate would break both.

O6_input_shapes: authentication plugin name mysql_clear_password as the server-advertised initial plugin (clear branch of the initial response)
transport: plain TCP / TLS with deferred self-signed fingerprint / sslMode=trust TLS / local unix socket
credential: non-empty password vs null or empty password (checked explicitly in the added condition)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second clear-password writer with no self-check at all, while its neighbour ClearPasswordPlugin has its own sslMode/fingerprint guard (src/main/java/org/mariadb/jdbc/plugin/authentication/addon/ClearPasswordPlugin.java:51-57)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer hardening the plugin layer would naturally mirror the ClearPasswordPlugin guard here, giving the same protection two inconsistent implementations.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third clear-password sink (full-auth 0x04 branch) gated by its own sslMode/sslFingerPrintValidation predicate rather than requireSecure()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already exists in-tree as a copy of the same write; a maintainer could extend or refactor this branch and silently drop the transport requirement.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new AuthenticationPluginFactory for a clear-text plugin (e.g. a 'pam' alias) that does not override requireSecure(), which defaults to false
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: requireSecure() is an opt-in default-false declaration (src/main/java/org/mariadb/jdbc/plugin/AuthenticationPluginFactory.java:37-39) and plugins are discovered by exact type string in ServiceLoader (src/main/java/org/mariadb/jdbc/plugin/authentication/AuthenticationPluginLoader.java:34-37), so a new clear-text plugin silently bypasses the gate.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the local-transport exemption names only UnixDomainSocket (src/main/java/org/mariadb/jdbc/client/impl/StandardClient.java:476), leaving the Windows named-pipe transport over-rejected
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: NamedPipeSocket is the sibling local transport and is still constructed for Windows pipes; a maintainer adding a local exemption would plausibly touch it.

O9_family: CWE-522 insufficiently protected credentials (clear-text password sent before peer identity is verified)

O10_build.project_tests: JUnit 5 unit tests under src/test/java/org/mariadb/jdbc/unit (client, plugin/authentication) run without a DB; the authentication integration tests (src/test/java/org/mariadb/jdbc/integration/ConnectionTest.java:915-960) need a live MariaDB server with PAM and env TEST_PAM_USER/TEST_PAM_PWD. The advisory's own regression test drives a loopback ServerSocket, so the behaviour is exercisable offline.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add or keep an SSL-capability / requireSecure guard in HandshakeResponse.encode (or harden ClearPasswordPlugin.process), which still leaks the password to a TLS peer whose certificate was only accepted by deferred fingerprint.

unverified: Repo size in MB could not be measured without a shell; tiny_repo/giant_repo therefore not assessed (source tree is large, several hundred Java files).
O8 is empty on the routes I traced, but I did not exhaustively prove that no third-party plugin registered through ServiceLoader reaches a clear-password write without the checks.
The fix commits are on two maintenance branches; the pinned tree corresponds to the second (factory-based requireSecure/isMitMProof) API, so the first commit's diff context does not apply verbatim.
